newsitem.title: FRANCE: Preussag sees sharp 1995/96 profit fall.
newsitem.headline: Preussag sees sharp 1995/96 profit fall.

text.p: German industrial group Preussag AG profits for the business year that ended on September 30 fell sharply from the previous year, the company's chairman told reporters late on Tuesday.

Speaking to reporters in Dijon, Michael Frenzel said results for the full year would correspond to the development in the first half, when profits plunged 30 percent. But he said shareholders would still be offered an "attractive" dividend.
Management board members who asked not to be identified said the decline in after-tax profit would be in double-digits.

Frenzel, attributing the earnings decline to weakness in the steel industry, said group sales in 1995/96 slipped to 25.1 billion marks from 26.3 billion, largely because of a fall in steel sales at Preussag's trading unit.
Group incoming orders rose to 30.2 billion marks from 28.5 billion and orders on hand fell slightly to 13.6 billion marks from 14 billion.
